topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: I suppose it's the sort of thing that happens. You shuffle through the clutter, the remnants of someone else's life, and there it is. A tattered teddy, its fur dulled by time, eyes clouded over. You pause. Memories, dusty and delicate, flutter at the edge of your mind. This wasn’t just any bear; it was a confidant, a silent keeper of secrets. A part of you wonders what led it here, to this patch of sunlit grass, surrounded by strangers. Yet, here you are, drawn by a thread of nostalgia. You pick it up, feel the weight of the past in your hands. It’s a time capsule, really, wrapped in faded cotton. You pay the asking price, a token exchange for a piece of your past. It’s not about the bear, not really. It’s about the memories it carries, the child you were.
